title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from the previous page. S is a base. E/S is a smooth proper genus-1 curve with an involution σ that acts as -1 on Pic^0. Equivalently, E = I ∧_V E_0, where E_0 is an elliptic curve, V = {}_2E_0, and I is a V-torsor; σ comes from x ↦ -x on E_0. Concretely, σx = a - x and I = {x : 2x = a}, which is the fixed locus of σ. V acts on E by translation, commuting with σ. Set X = E/σ and Σ = E_0/±1; both are P^1-bundles over S. V acts on X and X/V ≅ Σ (eq. 24).

On this page:
(1) The ramification divisor of E → X is I. This gives a V-equivariant map I → X (eq. 26).
(2) It is a monomorphism, because I lands in the open X* where V acts freely. A point x ∈ I with ξ·x̄ = x̄ would need 2x + ξ = a, but 2x = a forces ξ = 0.
(3) One is therefore in the situation of an earlier §2: a P^1-bundle X with a (projective) action of the Klein group V. That section gives:
- Σ ≅ Σ_J with J = V^* (Cartier dual, identified with V via the Weil pairing);
- I is the inverse image of a well-determined section of Σ_J^* = Σ_J \ D_J, namely the image of I in X/V;
- the inverse image Δ of the branch divisor D_J in X is the canonical 6-point configuration attached to a V-action on a P^1-bundle. Each nonzero ξ ∈ V acts as an involution with two fixed points, giving 3 × 2 = 6 points.
(4) Grothendieck then identifies Δ concretely inside E. Δ is (set-theoretically, at geometric points) the set of points with nontrivial stabilizer in V. A point x̄ ∈ X is fixed by ξ ≠ 0 iff x + ξ ∈ {x, a - x}. Translation by ξ is free, so x + ξ = a - x, i.e. 2x + ξ = a. Hence 4x = 2a but 2x ≠ a.

The next page completes the count. There are 16 points with 4x = 2a (a torsor under {}_4E_0); removing the 4 points of I leaves 12; dividing by σ leaves 6. Thus Δ is the image of the 'half-4-torsion' points modulo ±, the octahedral configuration. This is the classical picture that the order-4 points of an elliptic curve modulo ±1 form the 6 vertices of an octahedron: X(4) has genus 0 and symmetry group PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4.

Purpose: to describe moduli of genus-1 curves with such an involution (or elliptic curves with level structures) via P^1-bundles with Klein-group action and sections of Σ_J^*. This is a relative, Legendre-type parametrization valid over bases where 2 is invertible.
errors: The page says 'configuration icosaèdrale'. The configuration is 6 points, the fixed points of the three involutions of a Klein four-group acting on P^1, i.e. the octahedral vertices. The next page correctly says 'configuration octaédrale'. This is a slip, not a mathematical error.

Minor gap: the stabilizer argument is done only on geometric points ('ensemblistement'). Scheme-theoretic reducedness/étaleness of Δ over S needs 2 invertible, which the cote title assumes, but this is not stated here.

ideas.what: Genus-1 curve with an involution acting as -1 on Pic^0 written as a twist I ∧_V E_0 by a torsor under E_0[2]; the quotient X = E/σ is a P^1-bundle carrying a V-action with X/V ≅ E_0/±1
ideas.modern_name: Twists of elliptic curves by 2-torsion torsors; relative Kummer/Legendre picture; genus-1 double covers of conics
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Weber, Klein); relative version standard in the arithmetic of elliptic curves (e.g. Katz–Mazur style moduli)

ideas.what: Fixed locus of σ (= ramification of E→X) is the V-torsor I, which embeds into the free locus X*
ideas.modern_name: Weierstrass/branch points of a double cover as a 2-torsion torsor

ideas.what: Points of E with nontrivial V-stabilizer in X are those with 4x = 2a, 2x ≠ a; mod σ they give 6 points (octahedral configuration), the inverse image of the branch divisor D_J
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral configuration of 4-torsion mod ±1; genus-0 modular curve X(4) with S_4 symmetry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Klein (Vorlesungen über das Ikosaeder, modular curves of level 4)

deep.surprise_reason: A careful relative (over a base S) rendering of the classical link between 2- and 4-torsion of elliptic curves and Klein-group actions on P^1 with their octahedral configuration. Correct and neatly organized, but the content is classical (Klein, Legendre form, X(4)) and contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'est I, et on a un [-...-]morphisme' — reads 'et on a un' rather than 'et ... un'; the struck word precedes 'morphisme'.
'l'ouvert X^* de X (27)': the '(27)' is a forward-reference mark written above, not part of the sentence.
'la configuration icosaèdrale dans X, correspondant à l'action donnée de V sur la fibration en droites projectives X' — the transcription wrongly ends with 'V sur X'; the fibration is X, not V.
Line 'En dessous de l'action de V sur X, Δ ... se récupère comme le diviseur de ramification ...': the phrase reads 'se récupère comme le diviseur de ramification'.
'il correspond donc aux pts (à valeurs dans des corps alg. clos) dont le stabilisateur dans V est ≠ 0'.
'ξ ∈ V = {}_2E_0, ξ ≠ 0' and 'x + ξ ∈ {x, σx = a - x}'; final line 'd'où 4x = 2a, mais 2x ≠ a'.
